page: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but features a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m8g.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, particularly in memory bandwidth and multi-threaded processing. It achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark database operations. Memory read-only bandwidth reaches up to 10692.66 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 897.11 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category.

This server is highly suited for highly parallelized, memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing. Its performance in Redis SET operations is exceptionally strong, reaching 360.85 million operations per second. Conversely, the server is less optimal for workloads requiring hardware acceleration or local high-speed storage, as it lacks GPUs and local NVMe drives. LLM text generation speeds also rank on the lower end, making it less suitable for real-time generative AI inference compared to GPU-accelerated alternatives.
